title: Singleton Fourier coefficient under the balanced lift
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Define a function on $\{-1,1\}^{n+1}$ by $F(z)=z_0 f((z_0z_1,\ldots,z_0z_n))$. Then the Fourier coefficient of $F$ at the singleton coordinate $i+1$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a nonnegative integer
$f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$i$ is a coordinate in the $n$-dimensional cube
